text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Cyprus issue can be dealt with and the United States is willing to take on a more active role if asked, says a U.S. State Department official.

- Disclosures that the recently retired Greek area manager of cash-strapped Cyprus Airways received the inflated salary of 75,000 pounds ($150,000) annually shocks many senior executives of the company.
- Russian and American businesses have expressed interest in re-operating a fertilizer factory owned by the Hellenic Mining Company.
- The United Nations is willing to call for direct talks between the two sides in Cyprus provided this will lead to further negotiations.
- A 14-year-old burnt down his school canteen because its goods were more expensive than other shops.
- The Cyprus pound is in high demand in the occupied north, and is used mainly for smuggling.
